title: Online Couples Therapy UK | Therapy with Roy | Roy Lam MBACP
description: Online couples therapy with Roy Lam, MBACP. UK-based, available worldwide. English and Cantonese. 50-minute video sessions, £120. Free consultation.

hero.eyebrow: Online couples therapy · UK-based, available worldwide
hero.subtitle: A confidential, non-judgemental space for partners facing difficulties to communicate better, understand each other and decide how to move forward together.

problem.label: When couples come to therapy
problem.title: Whatever has brought you here
paragraphs: Couples reach out for many reasons: the same argument on repeat, feeling distant from each other, a loss of trust, or pressure from work, family and life changes. Some are not sure whether they want to stay together at all.
Together we create a space where each of you can be heard, and where you can begin to understand the patterns that have developed between you. You do not need to be at breaking point to ask for help.
problem.quote: “I look forward to providing my support to you and helping you reflect, connect and grow.”

steps.title: Free Consultation
steps.text: Book a free 15–30 minute call. We’ll talk about what’s brought you here and whether we’re a good fit. No commitment required.

steps.title: Your First Session
steps.text: We meet online via Google Meet, Monday to Friday, 9am–7pm London time. Sessions are 50 minutes, and each of you has the chance to share what you would like to change.

steps.title: Reflect & Grow
steps.text: Over time, work together on how you communicate, handle conflict and reconnect, at a pace that suits you both.

approach.title: Integrative and tailored to you both
paragraphs: My approach is integrative and tailored to each couple. I draw on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Emotion-Focused Therapy and Bowen’s Family Systems Theory, combining evidence-based techniques with a warm, genuinely non-judgemental presence.

Originally from Hong Kong, I have a particular understanding of the cultural pressures that many East Asian and immigrant communities face, including the tension between family expectations and personal identity. I offer sessions in both English and Cantonese.
I am a registered member of the BACP (No. 397064) with a Master of Social Sciences in Counselling from the University of Hong Kong.
